title: Autoscale interlock, ramping commitments, and error-budget credit language for Dedicated throughput
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Draft contract-ready SLA and remediation language that binds Dedicated throughput commitments to concrete autoscaling interlock behavior, controlled ramp rates, and an error-budget-driven credit schedule. Scope includes definitions, measurement window, ramp policy for capacity restores, autoscale-trigger blackouts, and credit computation that accounts for both throughput degradation and prolonged autoscale recovery. This ticket is intended for PM->Legal->Engineering->Finance alignment and should result in a templated SLA clause customers can opt into for Reserved GPU pools.
background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity ask for both guaranteed throughput and predictable failure remediation. Historically our SLA language covered throughput percentiles and simple credit formulas but did not specify autoscale ramp behavior, temporary throttling windows during healing, or how credits are computed when autoscaler recoveries are rate-limited. That omission has led to ambiguous post-incident negotiations and inconsistent credit outcomes. We need unambiguous contractual language that ties operational controls (autoscale ramp rate, warm pool behavior, cross-AZ failover) to credits and notice procedures.
acceptance_criteria: A concise SLA clause (<= 350 words) that defines Throughput Guarantee, Measurement Window, and Error Budget in plain language
A deterministic credit formula that maps measured shortfalls and prolonged degradations to percentage-of-monthly-credit, with worked examples for 1-hour, 6-hour, and 7-day degradations
Explicit autoscale interlock and ramping policy text (max scale-up rate in vCPUs/GPU units per minute, warm-pool burst windows) suitable for inclusion in contract addendum
Agreement from Engineering on metric definitions (metric names, aggregation, and computation lookback) and from Finance on credit caps
A one-page operational playbook for SRE/Support to compute credits during incidents, including required evidence (time-series, trace IDs, capacity change logs)
proposed_sla_definitions: Throughput Entitlement: Customer is entitled to N tokens-per-minute (TPM) averaged over a 30-day billing cycle as defined in the order form. For short-term window SLOs, we specify Throughput Percentile measured by p95 of successful request throughput sampled in 1-minute buckets.

Measurement Window: Default windows are 1 hour, 24 hours, and 30 days. Credits are computed using the worst-case window where entitlement is not met, with prorated application as listed in the credit matrix.

Error Budget: For a given window W, error_budget_remaining = max(0, entitlement - observed_effective_throughput). Observed effective throughput excludes traffic blocked by customer-configured rate limits and requests that failed pre-ingress (e.g., auth failures).

Autoscale Interlock: During capacity shortages, Redwood will attempt automated scale-up subject to a ramping limit (see Ramp Policy below). Autoscale interlock describes conditions where the autoscaler will fallback to a conservative ramp to protect cluster stability (e.g., rapid OOM cascades) and when manual escalation is required.

Degraded State: A degraded state exists when observed_effective_throughput < 95% of entitlement for at least 5 consecutive minutes. Sustained degradation is when the threshold is breached for greater than 6 hours.

Service Credit: Financial credit applied to customer invoice when sustained degradation thresholds are met, calculated per the Credit Formula section. Credits are the exclusive monetary remedy under the SLA.
autoscale_ramp_policy: Ramp Policy (contract language): Redwood will restore capacity at a maximum rate of 10% of the customer's reserved GPU pool per minute, subject to a minimum step of 1 GPU unit. If restoring at that rate would exceed provider-imposed device allocation limits or create cross-AZ imbalance, Redwood may apply a capped ramp of 5% per minute and will notify customer within the incident timeline specified below.

Warm-pool burst: For customers who purchase 'warm-pool' add-on, Redwood will allow a one-time instantaneous burst of up to 25% of reserved capacity within a 60-second window for immediate mitigation. Use of warm-pool burst resets a 24-hour cooldown for subsequent bursts.

Autoscale trigger blackout: After a large-scale recovery (>50% of pool restored within 10 minutes), the autoscaler will enter a 5-minute stabilization blackout where additional automated scale decisions are paused to prevent oscillation. During blackout, manual ops actions are allowed and visible in event logs.

Manual escalation: If autoscaler is unable to increase capacity to 50% of entitlement within 30 minutes, Redwood engineering will open a priority incident and provide hourly status updates. This boundary is used to escalate contractual remedies.
credit_formula_and_examples: Credit Basis: Credits are computed on a percentage of the monthly Dedicated subscription fee for the affected resource pool. CreditPercent is computed from the normalized shortfall across the applicable measurement window.
Step 1 - Shortfall Rate: shortfall_rate = 1 - (observed_effective_throughput / entitlement) capped at 1.0.
Step 2 - Window Weighting: apply a tapering weight for longer windows (W): weight(W) = min(1.0, ln(1 + duration_hours) / ln(1 + 168)). Example weights: 1-hour=0.12, 24-hour=0.55, 168-hour(7d)=1.0.

Step 3 - Autoscale recovery adjustment: recovery_penalty = max(0, 1 - min(1, time_to_restore_minutes / 60)). This reduces credits if autoscale restored quickly. For manual escalations, recovery_penalty = 0.
Final Credit % = min(CreditCap, round(shortfall_rate * weight(W) * (1 - recovery_penalty) * 100, 2))
CreditCap: default 30% of monthly fee for any single incident; aggregate cap for a billing month is 60%.

Worked example A (1-hour spike): entitlement 10k TPM, observed 7.5k TPM for one hour. shortfall_rate=0.25, weight(1h)=0.12, time_to_restore=15m => recovery_penalty=0.75. Final Credit% = 0.25*0.12*(1-0.75)=0.0075 => 0.75% => rounds to 1% credit applied to monthly invoice.

Worked example B (6-hour sustained): entitlement 10k TPM, observed 6k TPM for 6 hours. shortfall_rate=0.4, weight(6h)=0.38, time_to_restore=240m => recovery_penalty=0.0 (manual escalation), Final Credit% = 0.4*0.38*1=15.2% => 15.2% credit (subject to CreditCap).
evidence_and_dispute_process: Required Evidence: time-series of throughput (1m buckets), autoscaler activity logs, allocation events, and relevant traces or request IDs for a representative 5-minute sample during the event window.
Customer claim timeline: Customer may submit a credit claim within 30 days of incident end. Redwood will validate within 10 business days, during which both parties can supply additional evidence.
Dispute resolution: If disagreement persists, the parties escalate to the partnership review committee. Credits are applied prospectively to the next billing cycle unless otherwise agreed.
Transparency: Redwood will provide a post-incident report for any incident that triggered credits, detailing timeline, root cause (if known), and remediation steps.
operational_playbook_for_support: Step 0 - Triage: Confirm observed throughput vs entitlement using metric 'dedicated.pool.throughput.1m' and verify customer-configured limits haven't been exceeded.
Step 1 - Autoscale history: Pull 'autoscaler.events' for +/-1 hour around degradation. Note ramp rates applied and any errors (allocation failures, AZ capacity shortages).

Step 2 - Apply ramp policy rules: Verify whether ramping adhered to contractual caps. If ramping was constrained by provider limits, mark the incident as 'provider-limited' and notify customer in the PIR.
Step 3 - Compute credit draft: Use standardized spreadsheet (link in links) to fill shortfall, window, weight, recovery time and produce Draft Credit Percent and dollar amount.
Step 4 - Communication: Share draft with customer within 10 business days. After validation, schedule credit application on next invoice.
decisions: Use p95 of 1-minute throughput buckets as the canonical short-term throughput SLO metric (approved by Eng)
Adopt tiered weight function for window tapering to balance short spikes vs sustained degradations
Warm-pool burst will be offered as a billable add-on; default customers do not receive immediate burst capability
open_questions: Legal: Is the CreditCap and aggregate monthly cap acceptable? Legal and Finance need final sign-off.
Engineering: Can autoscaler telemetry reliably record 'time_to_restore_minutes' with +/- 1 minute accuracy?
Sales: Do we need a simplified one-paragraph SLA variant for self-serve customers that omits ramp policy details?
Ops: Are there provider partner constraints (cloud quotas) that should be surfaced to customers in order forms?
